observations: body L1-L6: the proportion begun on p. 315. The minus signs are printed as dashes (9.6 to 10.4 pt), that of L6 shorter (5.4 pt), and are set as minus signs. With six temporal hours to the semidiurnal arc, distance of A from the meridian : semidiurnal arc of A = hours of distance of A : 6, so L6 follows from L3, as printed.

body L7-L11: the minus signs of L11 are printed as dashes (9.0 to 10.0 pt). The semidiurnal arc is 90° plus the ascensional difference, and in the eastern hemisphere the oblique ascension of a star of northern declination is less than its right ascension by that difference; so semid. A − semid. B = (asc. recta A − asc. recta B) − (asc. obliq. A − asc. obliq. B) = α − β, and the right side of L11 is printed with the opposite sign. The rule (α) agrees with α − β: it gives α when A is on the meridian and β when A is on the horizon (six temporal hours), as it must, while the identity as printed would give 2α − β there. The printed form is kept.

body L12-L14: «al–Battānī» (L13) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.6 pt). With (α − β) for (β − α) when α > β and the sign − before it, the rule is in both cases directio = α + (β − α) × horae : 6.

body L15-L28: the figure of the sphere stands on the left of L15-L28, redrawn from the print: the horizon, the circle of position NAS, the equator and the ecliptic as circles fitted to the printed strokes (rms 0.33 to 0.40 pt), the meridian NS as a straight stroke; the dashed parallels F″F′, E″E′ and the dashed circles of declination from P through B, C, A, E″ and F″ are fitted to their dashes and drawn dash by dash; the arcs bc of the equator and BC of the parallel E″E′ are printed bold; the points P, A, B are marked by dots. The words meridianus, ecliptica, aequator and horizon are set along their lines; the sign of Aries stands on the meeting of the equator and the ecliptic. The minus signs of L15-L17 are printed as dashes (10.0 to 10.2 pt). «al–Battānī» (L25) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt); «16–20» (L26) has a long dash (4.2 pt). The place is p. 134, L16-L20 of the translation («Si duo gradus illi in duobus diversis hemisphaeriis sunt...»).
body L29-L33: «309–10» has a long dash (5.2 pt).

notes_left L1-L6: the end of Schiaparelli's note 3 begun on p. 315. «Schiaparelli» is set in small capitals and divided between L4 and L5, as printed; the dash before it measures 7.0 pt. «Ptolemaeum», divided between L5 and L6, is letter-spaced.
notes_left L7-L10: «132-33» has a hyphen (3.2 pt).

notes_right L1-L8: the closing parenthesis of «(2)» prints broken. The corrections of note 2 are those of Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXII), recorded on p. 133, L29 and L31 of the translation; the dash after «deprehendes.» measures 5.0 pt, a long dash. The opening parenthesis of «(3)» prints broken.
